statement: Open the project's unnamed default orthographic 3D view, with its camera above the southeast corner aimed at the ground-floor centre; renaming it makes the next invocation open a fresh unnamed view.
superiority: Open huge models instantly with progressive loading of geometry.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Default 3D View is orthographic (not strictly isometric); orbit/section box are separate features; behaviour of unnamed view omitted. Acceptance sketch: Default 3D view contains all visible model categories and a bounding box matches the model.

statement: Place a perspective camera from a plan, section or elevation view by clicking an eye point and a target point, with a level-relative height offset; the field of view is adjusted afterwards through the crop region.
superiority: Adjust the camera live while viewing the plan with a floating preview.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Field of view is not set at placement; it is edited via the crop region afterwards. Acceptance sketch: Camera view of a known box shows the expected perspective vanishing geometry.

statement: Define a camera path with keyframes and play or export a walkthrough animation.
superiority: Allow path editing in 3D with smooth spline and speed curves.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Walkthrough has the set frame count and passes the keyframe positions.

statement: Create a section view by drawing a cut line with direction, depth and extent.
superiority: Place sections with live preview and auto-name them by sheet convention.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Section of a known wall shows the wall profile with the correct cut elevation.

statement: Create a callout to define a detail region of a parent view at a different scale.
superiority: Reuse callout detail templates across multiple regions.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Callout region scales to the new view scale and shows the parent geometry.

statement: Place an elevation marker to create interior or exterior elevation views.
superiority: Auto-create the four interior elevations of a room in one click.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Elevation on a wall shows the face with correct projection.

statement: Create a floor plan view per level with its own view range, discipline and underlay settings.
superiority: Create plans for all levels at once from a naming rule.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Plan of level 2 cuts at the view range cut plane height and shows elements below it.

statement: Create a reflected ceiling plan per level showing ceilings, lights and grids above the cut plane.
superiority: Create the ceiling plan together with the floor plan on request.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Ceiling plan lists ceilings above the cut plane and not the floors.

statement: Create a structural plan view per level whose view direction type setting can look down (foundations) or up (framing), showing structural members.

source.ref: Set the View Direction in a Structural Plan View

superiority: Create structural plan sets for all levels and areas in one step.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Page documents the structural plan View Direction (Up/Down) type property; the 'symbolic display' part belongs to framing family settings, not the view. Acceptance sketch: Structural plan shows beams with their symbolic style at coarse detail.

statement: Define a region of a plan with its own view range to show elements at another height.
superiority: Edit region with live preview.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Region shows elements cut at its own cut plane.

statement: Create a 2D view for drawing details independent of the model.
superiority: Link drafting views to library for reuse.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Drafting view holds only 2D elements.

statement: Duplicate a view as a simple copy, with detailing, or as a dependent view linked to its parent.
superiority: Keep dependent views in sync with parent annotation edits.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Dependent view changes when the parent crop changes; independent copy does not.

statement: Create a legend view showing components, symbols and key information.
superiority: Auto-build legend from model types.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Legend lists each component once.

statement: Assign a view to a scope box so its crop region follows the box edits.
superiority: Reassign many views to a scope box by drag and drop in the browser.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Moving the scope box moves the crop of every assigned view.

statement: Create a sheet with title block, placed views and schedules.
superiority: Auto-lay out views on the sheet from rules.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Sheet shows placed views at set scale.

statement: Place views on sheets with viewport types, titles, and alignment guide grids.
superiority: Auto-arrange views to avoid overlaps and fit the title block.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Viewport centres at the placed point and title text is correct.

statement: Define viewport types that pick the view title type, show or hide the title and its extension line, and set that line's weight, colour and pattern.
superiority: Standards-based types from a template.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Viewport type controls title and extension line, not view 'extent'. Acceptance sketch: Viewport displays the title per type.

statement: Place a guide grid on sheets to align view placement.

source.ref: Video: Use Guide Grids to Align Views

superiority: Persistent alignment guides across sheets.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Viewports snap to the grid.

statement: Place a title block family on sheets with project parameters.

source.ref: About Title Block Information for Sheets

superiority: Fully parametric title blocks with automatic fit.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Title block shows project name and sheet number.

statement: Group sheets into named sheet collections via a sheet parameter, and organize the project browser by grouping and sorting views, sheets and schedules on selected properties up to six levels deep.
superiority: Saved browser organisations as shareable views.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Sheet Collections are named groupings (drag/drop or Sheet Collection parameter); Browser Organization is a separate grouping/sorting/filter feature; 'series' is not a documented grouping. Acceptance sketch: Browser tree reflects grouping rules.

statement: Show revision clouds and revision schedules on sheets with issue data.
superiority: Automatic revision tracking from diffs.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Revision schedule matches the clouds.

statement: Arrange open views in tiled or tabbed windows with switching.
superiority: Persist workspace layouts.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Windows tile in a grid.

statement: Close all open views except the active one in each tile (views moved outside the main window stay open), reducing memory use.
superiority: Auto-close idle views.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Command is named Close Inactive Views, not 'Close Hidden'; documented on the Drawing area page (View tab > Windows panel). Acceptance sketch: After close only one remains.

statement: Open a second window onto the same view so you can pan and zoom independently.
superiority: Link the two windows so a cursor in one is mirrored in the other.
notes: UNVERIFIED 2026-11-14: Searched help for replicate/replicate window/window tile/windows panel and API index; the Drawing area page lists Switch Windows, Tab, Tile, Close Inactive and User Interface but no Replicate command, though the feature plausibly exists in the Windows panel. Acceptance sketch: Two windows show the same view with different zoom.

statement: Show or hide panels like the Project Browser, Properties and status bar.
superiority: Saved workspace presets.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Hidden panel disappears.

statement: Orient the 3D view with the ViewCube and navigate with steering wheels (orbit, pan, walk, look, rewind).
superiority: Customisable navigation to match other CAD tools.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: ViewCube face click aligns to the face direction.

statement: Zoom, pan and fit views with mouse and keyboard shortcuts.
superiority: Consistent shortcuts configurable.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Zoom to fit shows entire model within window.

statement: Limit the 3D view to a box that clips the model on six sides.
superiority: Box handles snap to levels and grids.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Elements outside the box are hidden.

statement: Crop a view to a region that limits visible content and can hide the boundary.
superiority: Resize with numeric input and persist to templates.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Cropped view shows only elements inside.

statement: Temporarily hide or isolate elements or categories in the active view.

source.ref: Temporarily Hide or Isolate Elements or Element Categories

superiority: Persist as named presets.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Isolate shows only selected elements until reset.

statement: Show elements hidden in a view with a highlight to unhide them.
superiority: List hidden elements with reasons.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Hidden elements show in magenta.

statement: Display all lines at the thinnest weight to inspect geometry at high zoom.
superiority: Toggle per view and keep in view templates.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Lines draw at one pixel width regardless of line weight.

statement: Show or remove hidden lines for 2D representations of model geometry.
superiority: Per element line style settings.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Hidden lines appear dashed.

statement: Edit the cut profile of an element in a section to change its cut shape in the view.

source.ref: Change the Cut Profile of Elements

superiority: Preserve edits through geometry changes.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Edited cut profile shows in the view only.

statement: Render a 3D view with lighting, materials and settings to produce a picture.
superiority: GPU path tracing with progressive denoising in the viewport.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Rendered image matches resolution setting.

statement: Save rendered images into the project as lightweight rendering views listed under Renderings in the browser, where they can be placed on sheets; full-quality output goes through image export.

source.ref: Save the Rendered Image as a Project View

superiority: Cloud-less gallery with comparisons.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: No 'Render Gallery' feature found in 2027 help; project-stored renderings are saved views, with no documented compare function. Acceptance sketch: Gallery lists renders.

statement: Isolate the selected elements in a 3D view (the current isometric view or the default 3D view) by applying a resizable section box around them.

source.ref: Isolate Elements in a 3D View with a Selection Box

superiority: Keep the box live so it follows selection changes.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Selection Box applies a section box to the 3D view around the selection; it does not create a separate view. Acceptance sketch: View bounds equal the selection bounds plus the offset.

statement: Step backward or forward through previously visited view positions using the Rewind navigation-history tool available on every SteeringWheel.

source.ref: Retrieve Previous Views from the Navigation History

superiority: Persist history across sessions and bookmark views.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: History is the SteeringWheels Rewind tool, not a standalone 3D camera-history control. Acceptance sketch: Rewind restores the previous camera eye and target within 1e-6.

statement: Copy a primary view's dependent-view and crop configuration onto other parallel views of the same scale in one step.
superiority: Preview the generated dependent views and handle differing scales or crops automatically.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-14: feature found documented in Revit 2027 help during the verification pass; not in the original register Acceptance sketch: Set up two dependent views on one plan, apply to three other plans, and verify new dependents appear under each primary view.

statement: Save a view's position on a sheet with an anchor (view origin, center or corners) and assign it to other views so they land in the same place across sheets.

source.ref: View to Sheet Positioning and Automated Placement

superiority: Offer automatic layout and snap-to-saved-position suggestions when placing many similar views.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-14: feature found documented in Revit 2027 help during the verification pass; not in the original register Acceptance sketch: Save a position, assign it to a second plan on another sheet, and confirm both align when placed.

statement: Pin a viewport or schedule on a sheet so it cannot be moved by accident, and unpin it later.

superiority: Show which sheet items are pinned at a glance and allow pinning many at once.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-14: feature found documented in Revit 2027 help during the verification pass; not in the original register Acceptance sketch: Pin a viewport, try to drag it (blocked), unpin and drag successfully.

statement: Replace the view shown in a viewport with another compatible view from a searchable list while keeping the viewport at its center or view origin.
superiority: Preview the replacement and carry over the viewport type and title automatically.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-14: feature found documented in Revit 2027 help during the verification pass; not in the original register Acceptance sketch: Swap two plans on a sheet, confirm placement is preserved per positioning setting.

statement: Apply a view template's properties to every view currently placed on a sheet in one step, without assigning the template.

superiority: Report which views changed and provide a one-step undo.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-14: feature found documented in Revit 2027 help during the verification pass; not in the original register Acceptance sketch: Apply a scale-only template to a sheet with three views; all three show the same scale and none stays linked.

statement: Break a section line in a given view so the line does not cross the drawing while the section's displayed content is unchanged.
superiority: Allow the break to be remembered per sheet viewport as well as per view.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-14: feature found documented in Revit 2027 help during the verification pass; not in the original register Acceptance sketch: Break a section line in a plan; verify the section view content is unchanged and rejoin restores the line.

superiority: Accept arbitrary curves with live preview of the cropped content.

statement: Snap a view title, or its extension line, to view boundaries, crop regions, title-block geometry, sheet elements and guide grids without first selecting the viewport, with extension-line grips showing as soon as the title is selected.
superiority: Show snap candidates as ghosted guides before the click.

superiority: Support all common 6-DOF controllers through a documented open interface.
